text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency postponed signing a deal for the sale of a 70 percent stake in the state cement maker Devnya Cement to Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex because the necessary bank guarantees had not been received by the central bank by Monday's deadline, the agency's executive director Alexander Sabotinov said. @
-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said its foreign exchange reserves rose to $1,145.5 million at end-April from $554.3 million a month earlier.
-- The BNB said it would put into circulation on Thursday a 50,000-lev note, the largest denomination to go in use so far.
-- Bulgaria's state owned Biochim Bank posted a zero net profit last year after setting aside 66.5 billion levs for provisions, a Biochim senior official said.
-- Bulgaria's Trade minister Daniela Bobeva said 919 firms from 37 countries were taking part at the annual trade fair in Plovdiv which opened on Monday. @

-- A technical mission of the International Monetary Fund arrived on Monday in Sofia to discuss legislative draft amendments which should facilitate the introduction of a fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board system, in the country.

-- A Bulgarian delegation is expected to visit Syria to discuss repayment of Syria's $14 million debt to Bulgaria, Trade minister Daniela Bobeva said. Bulgaria is expected to propose debt for equity swap or debt for concessions swap. @

-- The Sofia City Court postponed ruling on an insolvency suit against the state owned Balkanbank filed by the central bank because experts' report on Balkanbank's financial status has not been submitted in due time, a court official said.
-- Bulgaria's National Social Insurance Institute said it would propose to the cabinet to raise pensions by 16 percent from June.
-- Bulgaria exported oil products worth $275 million last year, which made up six percent of the country's total exports, private Balkan agency said, quoting Trade ministry officials. @
-- Bulgaria's monthly inflation for April was expected at between two to four percent against 12.3 percent in March, experts said.
